author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking. The correction updates that visit in place, never adds another, and returns to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when its correction is opened (GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit), then the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, model attribute `visit`) shows that visit's current date and description.

[REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted (POST to the same URL), then that visit is updated in place, the pet gains no additional visit, and the owner's record is shown (redirect to the owner detail page).

[REQ-VIS-003] given a blank description or a date of today or earlier, when a visit correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is redisplayed naming the field, and the stored visit is unchanged.
[REQ-VIS-003] edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not exist or does not belong to the named pet is refused, and no visit changes.
[REQ-VIS-003] edge case 4: correcting a visit for a pet that does not belong to the named owner is refused, and no visit changes.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5 as narrowed, NG-4).
Any link or button on the owner detail page leading to the correction: the form is reachable by its URL alone, per the owner's decision; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.
Relaxing the booking date rule for corrections: a correction must carry a date later than today, as at booking (open question recorded in docs/prd.md).
Changing which pet a visit belongs to, or any visit field beyond date and description.
notes: Scoping edits (uncommitted, this dispatch): docs/prd.md adds REQ-VIS-003 to Visits (Done-when bullets, edge cases 3-5, ADR link) and narrows the NG-5 row, the Non-Goals preamble, and two Open Questions. New non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-30-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md. docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md status line notes the NG-5 narrowing. docs/adr/README.md index lacks a row for the new ADR; that file is outside product write scope, so system-design-expert or root should add it. Narrowest readings taken where the intake is silent: (1) mismatched owner/pet/visit ids are refused and change nothing, which follows REQ-VIS-001 edge case 1; (2) no confirmation message is required on success, only the return to the owner's record; (3) a past-dated visit cannot be re-saved with its date, which is the literal consequence of 'validates like visit creation' and is recorded as an open question. The reused template's heading and submit wording for an edit are a design matter, bounded by REQ-LANG-002 (no hard-coded wording). Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the owner aggregate unchanged (system-design § Contracts invariants: Visit persists only by cascade from Owner through OwnerRepository). The adjustment mirrors the pet edit seam: PetController.findPet takes an optional petId path variable and returns a new Pet when it is absent (grep basis, IDE oracle not connected: PetController.java:75-87). VisitController.loadPetWithVisit takes an optional visitId path variable the same way. With no visitId it keeps today's behavior: a new Visit is added to the pet. With a visitId it resolves the owner (existing refusal), then the pet (existing refusal), then the visit through a new Pet lookup by identity mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). An absent visit throws IllegalArgumentException, matching the existing owner and pet refusals (REQ-VIS-001 edge case 1 precedent). New handlers: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit. POST applies the same non-future-date rejection as processNewVisitForm, factored into one private check both handlers call, then saves the owner and redirects to /owners/{ownerId}. On a binding or date error it redisplays pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm without saving. The loaded graph is detached (open-in-view disabled, § Persistence), so the stored visit stays unchanged. The template's submit label switches on visit['new'] between #{addVisit} and a new #{updateVisit} key, mirroring createOrUpdateOwnerForm.html:18. The key goes into all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002 bundle-parity test). Design-doc writes: REQ-VIS-003 joins the Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController Contracts rows; the Threat Model mass-assignment row records the visit field allow-list; a new § Scale and Load section carries the correction-lookup row.
integration_points: Binding target for the new POST .../visits/{visitId}/edit entry point: the persisted Visit resolved through Owner -> Pet by identity, behind an allow-list. The controller's @InitBinder keeps setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") (security-principles § Mass assignment) and adds setAllowedFields("date", "description"). The allow-list also covers the booking path, where it is behavior-preserving because the form posts only those two Visit properties. It makes the PRD non-goal 'no visit field beyond date and description' true at binding.

Repository boundary double: extend the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository fixture in VisitControllerTests (@WebMvcTest slice). Reason: the web slice loads no JPA, and a hand-written double would have to implement the whole JpaRepository surface for five controller tests (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: tolerated framework stub). Prove in-place update and 'no visit changes' through the stub: on success, capture the saved Owner and assert the pet's visit count is unchanged and the visit with that id carries the new values; on every refusal, assert save is never called.
Framework transport double: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-layer harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).
Fixture: the test owner's pet needs one persisted-looking Visit with an id set, so the edit paths have something to resolve.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: docs/system-design.md:90 assigns 'finds one of them by identity' to Pet, a seam below the web boundary. author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Missing boundary validation on the new correction POST: a request with an empty date parameter (date=) binds null onto the persisted Visit, because Spring's formatter parses blank text to null. The guard `if (visit.getDate() != null && !visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now()))` (VisitController.java:144) skips null, and Visit.date has no @NotNull (Visit.java:38-40 carries only @Column and @DateTimeFormat). visit_date is nullable in every schema (`visit_date  DATE,` at db/h2/schema.sql:61, db/postgres/schema.sql:50, and db/mysql/schema.sql:53). processEditVisitForm then saves the owner, erasing the booked visit's date. Attacker path: an unauthenticated POST to /owners/{o}/pets/{p}/visits/{v}/edit with date= and any non-blank description. This contradicts REQ-VIS-003, which requires a date later than today for a correction (prd.md:113-114, edge case 5), and the trust-boundary rule to validate shape before use (security-principles § Trust Boundaries). The booking path already accepted a null date before this change, and the shared helper now covers both routes. This slice extends that gap to overwriting an existing record, so the new reach sets severity: an integrity loss, not a confidentiality or code-execution issue. Class sweep: `grep -rn -F 'rejectValue("date"' src/main/java` finds this one site only.
findings.fix: On the correction path, reject a null date alongside a non-future one. For example, processEditVisitForm rejects `visit.getDate() == null` with result.rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate") before the hasErrors check. Add an empty-date row to the invalidCorrections test source. Leave the booking route unchanged in this slice: hardening it is REQ-VIS-001 behavior, and a separate PRD question if it is wanted.

approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the controller-wide @InitBinder keeps setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") and adds setAllowedFields("date", "description") (VisitController.java:53-54). Because it applies to every model attribute in the controller, it also narrows the @ModelAttribute Owner that both POST handlers bind, so the hidden petId and any posted owner, pet, or id fields are ignored. This is stricter than the baseline.

Ownership: the visit resolves by identity through the owner's pet (owners.findById, then owner's pet, then Pet.getVisit, VisitController.java:68-86), so every request re-resolves the entity. An unknown visit, another pet's visit, or a pet that does not belong to the owner is refused before binding. Tests cover all three (theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAVisitNotBelongingToThePet with UNKNOWN_ID and OTHER_PETS_VISIT_ID, and theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAPetNotBelongingToTheOwner). Pet.getVisit excludes new (unsaved) visits.

Error disclosure: the new IllegalArgumentException message carries only the numeric path ids (VisitController.java:82-83) and matches the existing owner and pet refusals, so it adds no stored data to the error page (known defect, unchanged).

Output escaping: the template change uses th:text with message-bundle keys only (createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:39-40). The diff adds no th:utext or preprocessing `__${` (grep -F over the added lines found none). The ten added updateVisit values are plain text.
Secrets: grep -F for password, token, secret, and apikey over the added lines of the change set found no matches.

Supply chain: the change touches no build files (git diff HEAD -- build.gradle settings.gradle is empty). Resolved runtimeClasspath: spring-boot-starter-webmvc 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5, thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured, so no NVD match ran in this review.
Refusal path: spring.jpa.open-in-view=false (application.properties:11), and a refused correction never calls save, so the in-memory binding onto the entity is never flushed.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: The code change stays in one package (Pet.getVisit plus a new GET/POST edit route in VisitController); the other 18 files are one-line i18n keys, a one-line template label switch, and PRD/ADR/system-design edits. VisitController is a declared security surface, but the new route reuses the existing owner-then-pet lookup and saves only through OwnerRepository.

semantic_surprise.note: The @InitBinder change setAllowedFields("date", "description") applies to every binding in VisitController, including the existing booking POST and the @ModelAttribute Owner that is resolved from the model and bound from request params. That silently changes REQ-VIS-001 behaviour: owner fields posted to /visits/new were bindable before and are now ignored. It tightens security, but it is a behaviour change on a route the slice does not name, and no booking-route test pins it. Also by design: correcting a past visit's description forces the date forward (recorded as an open PRD question), and a rejected correction mutates the detached in-memory visit but never saves it.
